**WHO WE ARE**
==============

Lantern is building the AI-native operating system for the $9T wholesale distribution industry. Billions of dollars sit tied up in stock, yet most distributors still buy on gut feel and spreadsheets. We partner with leading distributors to deliver precise, AI-powered purchasing recommendations that drive 30% leaner inventory, 10% higher sales, and 20+ hours saved per week per user. We've gone from $0 to $5M ARR in 8 months, raised $7M from top VCs, and are hitting hypergrowth.

**THE ROLE**
============

We're hiring a Machine Learning Engineer to scale the core ML platform behind our product: the production systems that ingest operational data, train models, and generate recommendations. The central challenge is making these workflows scalable, repeatable, observable, and easy to operate across hundreds of customers. You'll own the platform end to end, from data ingestion through training pipelines to inference and monitoring in production. It's a high-ownership role on a small team, working directly with our CTO to ship systems every customer relies on.

**WHAT YOU'LL DO**
==================

* Own and scale the ML and data pipelines that power Lantern's customer recommendations.
* Build reusable infrastructure for data ingestion, feature generation, model training, validation, and output.
* Improve pipeline performance, reliability, and observability as Lantern scales across more customers.
* Build systems that catch data-quality issues, pipeline failures, and unexpected outputs before they reach customers.
* Turn customer-specific workflows into repeatable, configuration-driven systems, and help shape the platform architecture.

**WHAT YOU BRING**
==================

* 4–6 years as an ML or Software Engineer building ML systems in production.
* Strong software engineering fundamentals and clean, maintainable, production-grade code.
* Experience building and scaling ML training and inference pipelines, ideally multi-tenant or per-customer.
* Hands-on with Python, cloud infrastructure (AWS or GCP), and orchestration (Airflow, Kubeflow, or similar).
* Comfort with messy, real-world data.
* BS/MS in Computer Science or a related technical field.

**NICE TO HAVE**
================

* Supply chain, logistics, demand forecasting, or operations-adjacent experience.
* Time-series forecasting frameworks and traditional ML tools (XGBoost, LightGBM, scikit-learn).
* Prior early-stage startup experience where you wore multiple hats.

**WHAT YOU'LL GET**
===================

* A founding-era, high-impact role at a hyper growth startup.
* Own the ML platform that drives customer P&L on every account.
* Make a massive positive impact across our entire supply chain and economy.
* Competitive compensation: ~$200K base + meaningful equity.
* An office in San Francisco with a tight-knit founding team.

**WHAT WE VALUE**
=================

We hire operators who own outcomes, combining sharp judgment with pragmatic execution and a willingness to do the unglamorous work. Hard work, humility, customer obsession, and pride in a job well done: the values our customers live by, and the values we hire for.

Compensation Range: $200K

**Company Description**

Chooch helps build and run the best Computer Vision AI applications that make cameras intelligent, enhancing productivity & revenues, while reducing operational costs. Chooch has been named a leading computer vision platform by IDC.

**Role Description**

We are looking for a Machine Learning Engineer (US-based) to join our team. This is a full-time, hybrid role with frequent hands-on experience with customer projects in the Bay Area. The Machine Learning Engineer will be responsible for the successful design, accuracy, and backbone behind our Computer Vision AI applications. This includes data preparation, training, configuring neural networks, deploying networks in real customer locations, and refining computer vision algorithms for healthcare, manufacturing, and retail customers. This role requires frequent interaction with technical and non-technical customers while working closely within our solutions engineering teams. The Machine Learning Engineering role has opportunity to grow, lead technical projects, and improve current processes while providing meaningful feedback to our product and solutions teams.

**Product Description** Chooch AI is a computer vision platform that helps hospitals automate supply room monitoring and inventory management. Using fixed cameras and AI, the platform continuously tracks supplies in storage areas and updates on-hand counts in real time. When inventory levels fall below defined thresholds, replenishment orders are automatically generated and sent to ERP systems, eliminating manual counts and barcode scanning. Hospitals using Chooch AI significantly reduce critical stockouts, optimize inventory levels, and improve supply chain staff productivity. By turning supply rooms into self-managing systems, Chooch AI enables clinical and supply chain teams to focus more time on patient care.

Responsibilities/What you'll do at Chooch:

* Design, train and fine-tune models for object detection, classification, segmentation, tracking and anomaly detection on real customer video and images.
* Adapt pretrained and foundation models (YOLO-family detectors, ViTs, CLIP-style and vision-language models) to new customer use cases with limited labeled data.
* Own data pipelines end to end: curation, labeling guidelines, augmentation, synthetic data, and dataset versioning.
* Optimize models for production and edge hardware using quantization, pruning, distillation, ONNX export and TensorRT, hitting agreed latency and accuracy targets.
* Build evaluation suites with clear metrics (mAP, precision/recall, false-alarm rates per camera-hour) and catch regressions before release.
* Deploy and monitor models in production, diagnose drift and failure cases, and close the loop with retraining.
* Work with product, solutions engineers and customers to turn vague requirements into measurable model specs.
* Write clean, tested, reviewed code and contribute to shared ML tooling.

Nice to have

* Experience with vision-language models (CLIP, LLaVA-style models) or open-vocabulary detection.
* Multi-object tracking and video analytics (re-identification, action recognition, temporal models).
* Few-shot learning, active learning, or synthetic data generation for low-data domains.
* MLOps tooling: MLflow or Weights & Biases, Kubernetes, Triton Inference Server, CI/CD for models.
* Domain experience in Healthcare, retail and supply chain, manufacturing inspection, workplace safety or video surveillance.

Key Components

* Model Development and Optimization: Design, develop, and optimize machine learning models for computer vision applications.
* Data Management: Collaborate with ML engineers to ensure the collection, processing, and maintenance of high-quality datasets necessary for model training and testing.
* Algorithm Implementation: Implement state-of-the-art computer vision algorithms to improve system accuracy and performance in real-world scenarios.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely within the solutions engineering team to integrate machine learning models into the broader product and systems.
* On-Site Travel and Field Testing: Many of our projects are live deployments with major fortune 500 customers – testing new, innovative ML technologies. Traveling on site is sometimes needed to see the environment, test in the real-world, and ensure the technology is operating as expected.
* Performance Evaluation: Regularly evaluate the performance of computer vision models, using both qualitative and quantitative methods, and iterate to enhance accuracy and efficiency.
* Research and Innovation: Understanding of the latest developments in machine learning and computer vision, applying innovative approaches and technologies to solve complex challenges.
* Stakeholder Engagement: Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to understand their needs and translate them into effective technical solutions.
* Problem-Solving: Address and troubleshoot complex problems that arise during the development and deployment of computer vision systems.

The ideal candidate should be deeply passionate about machine learning and its real-world applications, particularly in improving and leveraging state-of-the-art neural networks to make an impact.

 **Requirements**  

* 3–5 years of industry experience building ML systems, with at least 2 years focused on computer vision.
* BS or MS in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Math or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
* Strong Python and hands-on experience with PyTorch (or TensorFlow) for training and debugging deep learning models.
* Shipped at least one computer vision model to production, and can explain the trade-offs made along the way.
* Solid grasp of CNN and transformer architectures for detection, segmentation and classification.

jobs.description:
**Normal Computing | Build with Us**
------------------------------------

Normal is an applied AI company solving the hardest problems in AI and silicon. We build foundational hardware and software for the semiconductor industry, critical AI infrastructure, and the broader systems that power our world, in partnership with the world's most advanced institutions. We work as one team across New York City, Silicon Valley (Mountain View), London, Copenhagen, and Seoul.

**The Role**
------------

Normal's hardware runs the most memory-bound parts of large-model inference inside memory itself, rather than shuttling weights to a processor. The software that makes this programmable doesn't exist yet in any standard form. Getting a model correct on that hardware is the frontend's job; making it fast is yours. Our hardware does not look like a CPU or GPU, so its compiler backend can't be borrowed from one. As a Compiler Engineer focused on the backend, you will help design and build the custom compilation that maps LLM inference onto it, from scheduling and memory planning to the code our hardware actually executes.

You will work at the boundary between the compiler and the hardware, closely enough to know when an optimization belongs at a different layer, or when the right answer is a new abstraction. Our chip is pre-silicon, so you will measure your work against our simulators and FPGA prototypes first, and against silicon as it arrives.

**What You Will Own**
---------------------

* **Code Generation**: Build the passes that turn lowered programs into the code our hardware executes, designing new compilation approaches where conventional ones don't fit. Success means correct, efficient code for every operation our models need.
* **Scheduling and Memory Planning**: Own how work and data are scheduled and placed across our hardware's resources, measured by utilization and end-to-end latency on LLM inference.
* **Fusion and Dispatch**: Own fusion and dispatch decisions for LLM inference, so the hardware spends its time computing rather than moving data.
* **Hardware Co-Design**: Work the abstraction layer between the compiler and the hardware, and feed compiler constraints back to our hardware architects while the design can still change.
* **Profiling and Validation**: Validate every optimization with measured results from simulators, FPGA prototypes, and then silicon, and maintain a performance regression suite the team trusts.
* **Cross-Team Handoffs**: Take lowered programs from our frontend compiler engineers, and decide with the team which operations the compiler generates and which use hand-tuned kernels.

**What Makes You a Great Fit**
------------------------------

* Deep experience with compiler optimization or code generation for accelerators or other non-CPU targets: scheduling, tiling, fusion, or resource allocation
* Comfort working close to hardware: you think in terms of memory bandwidth and utilization as well as asymptotic complexity
* Willingness to design compilation approaches from first principles when existing ones don't fit the hardware
* Track record of shipping optimizations that moved a measured performance number
* Comfort building software for hardware that is still evolving, from simulation through bring-up
* Fluency in Python, and familiarity with C, C++, or Rust

**Bonus Points**
----------------

* Experience with PyTorch's compilation stack (TorchDynamo, FX, Inductor, torch.export) or other ML compilers, such as IREE, TVM, or XLA
* Experience compiling for in-memory, spatial, or other non-von-Neumann compute targets
* Background in hardware design tools such as logic synthesis or place-and-route
* Experience building or using cycle-level or performance simulators to guide optimization decisions
* Contributions to open-source compiler or kernel infrastructure (e.g., PyTorch, Triton, TVM, MLIR, LLVM)
* Publishing or presenting compiler or performance work at venues such as MLSys, ASPLOS, or CGO
